knowledge_gaps: The sampler requires user IDs, but the documented loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative). A concrete training-worker integration must preserve user identity for history exclusions without changing the diagnostic loader contract; truncated sequences cannot reliably reconstruct users.

The proposed comparison potentially changes the loss, negative count, and exclusion policy together. Record the baseline objective and sampler explicitly; match exclusions across controls or describe the result as a combined intervention rather than a loss-only effect.

The scoring adapters, negative sampler, worker seeding, and checkpoint schedule remain placeholders. Reproducibility also requires deterministic per-worker streams and verification that additional sampling preserves sequence draws.

Historical combined_score values lack confirmed metric provenance and matched evaluation details. They cannot establish an architecture ranking or justify abandoning depth correction. Fix the supplied cold-start architecture explicitly and treat multi-negative training as a separate hypothesis.

Originality 2 is reasonable. Potential 7 is speculative because training misranking does not identify the held-out bottleneck. Difficulty 3 likely understates user-aware sampling integration, scorer compatibility, and runtime constraints.
Sixteen negatives increase scoring and embedding-gradient costs, but no measured throughput, peak memory, remaining budget, or complete four-category allocation is supplied.

Uniform candidate classification has no explicit forgetting mechanism and can still learn popularity shortcuts. Fixed-negative training diagnostics and permitted popularity-stratified analyses can support interpretation, but selection must remain pinned macro validation HR@10.

The references motivate the experiment but do not validate its exact sampling policy or negative count. Conditional bootstrap intervals must also explicitly acknowledge adaptive configuration and checkpoint selection.
